thread:
Maya (Marketing): hey team — prepping a short post + webinar slice for next week. need a small, fast sanity rerun to validate two marketing claims: 1) quantized coldstart token throughput improvement, 2) 95th-percentile latency <120ms for short prompts on the redwood-7b family. can eng/runtime run a tiny sweep and drop raw artifacts? we only need the minimal reproducible pack (configs, raw per-request latencies, and the warmup protocol). target deadline: EOD Thursday. :pray:

Sam (Runtime): quick q — which exact model + quant profile? and do you want coldstart only or coldstart + a short warmup run? also, how many sample prompts?

Maya (Marketing): model = redwood-7b-v2-q4_0 (the quantized variant we referenced). Please run: coldstart (first request after model load) + a 10-request short warmup sequence for the same cohort. sample set = 50 short prompts (we've used the "web-snippet-short" seed before). A/B required vs redwood-7b-v2 (fp16) for baseline.

Ava (EngRuntime): ok. we'll need the exact seed file (or paste the 50 prompts) and the invocation command. also confirm: single-host run preferred (to avoid cross-host variance), and GPU affinity is fine. do you want CPU-only baseline?

Maya (Marketing): single-host yes. GPU affinity ok. baseline = fp16 on same infra. not CPU.

Maya (Marketing): here's the prompt pack — paste into a file or curl payload: 
```json
["Summarize: How to reduce cold start latency for small prompt apps.", "Short reply: What's the fastest model for a chat widget?", "Explain in one sentence: prefix caching.", "List: 3 tips to keep latency under 150ms.", "Summarize: tradeoffs of quantization for inference"]
```
(we'll attach full 50 prompts to the ticket if helpful)

Sam (Runtime): perfect — we'll run 3 repeats per config (coldstart + warmup), capture raw per-request latency, tail percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache stats. can you confirm we should also include token-level breakdowns?

Maya (Marketing): token-level breakdowns would be great but optional — prioritize per-request latencies and the two comparison runs.

Leo (Product): ping — please pin the exact model git sha or build id in artifacts. marketing will call out the model variant explicitly.

Ava (EngRuntime): noted. we'll include runtime metadata: docker image tag, model-version, quant profile, and config flags. also will record env (region, instance type).

Sam (Runtime): ETA: ~24 hours start-to-finish. will post a short summary CSV + tarball with raw latencies and a 1-paragraph caveat list (sampling, variance, and any anomalous outliers). scheduling now.

benchbot: scheduled quick_sweep job id=qs-2026-09-14-77; runner=single-host-gpu; estimated runtime=45m. artifacts will be uploaded to /artifacts/qs-4300123456 when complete.

Maya (Marketing): amazing — thank you 🙏 . if anything looks off, we might ask for a second tiny rerun with longer warmup.

Sam (Runtime): will flag if the first pass has >10% variance across repeats. otherwise we'll attach the CSV + readme.

benchbot: job qs-2026-09-14-77 completed; artifacts: https://redwood-internal/artifacts/qs-4300123456 (raw_latencies.csv, summary.csv, run_metadata.json, README.md)

Maya (Marketing): perfect — grabbing artifacts now. I'll follow up if marketing needs a tighter Q/A or a short explainer blurb for the blog.
